newsitem.title: UK: UK's Co-op Bank reports 24 pct rise in profits.
newsitem.headline: UK's Co-op Bank reports 24 pct rise in profits.

text.p: Britain's Co-operative Bank Plc said on Wednesday it had increased pre-tax profits by 24 percent to 45.5 million pounds ($74.6 million) for 1996.
Last year the bank, which trumpets its ethical and environmental banking stance and has developed telephone and automated banking, reported pre-tax profits of 36.7 million pounds.
It said retail customer deposits had increased by 27 percent year-on-year and retail lending rose 16 percent in 1996.

Terry Thomas, the bank's managing director, said in a statement that its customer retail balances, service infrastructure, operational revenue and balance sheet had all increased significantly as a result of its expansion plans over recent years.

With total assets of 4.5 billion pounds the Co-operative Bank -- a wholly owned subsidiary of the Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) -- is the smallest of Britain's clearing banks and has three percent of the market.

Thomas, who retires from the bank later this year, said investment to ensure the bank was able to compete in the next century required considerable capital and revenue spending, leading to a higher cost-income ratio. But such spending could be reined in if required, he added. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 7717
